realism_constraints: No advanced forensic DNA or fingerprint analysis available
Communication limited to telephone and postal mail, no mobile phones or internet
Transportation by motor cars and motorcycles, but no modern surveillance technology
location: Chichester and surrounding Sussex countryside, England
crime_subtype: execution by guillotine in hidden cave

cast.name: Sir Gregory Penne
cast.public_persona: eccentric rich man and film studio patron

cast.name: Sampson Longvale
cast.role_archetype: eccentric old gentleman with secret identity

surface_summary: A series of gruesome murders involving decapitations are linked to a mysterious figure called the Head-Hunter. The investigation leads to a wealthy baronet, Sir Gregory Penne, and his trained orangutan Bhag, but the true culprit is a seemingly benign old gentleman, Sampson Longvale, who uses a hidden guillotine in caves beneath his house to execute victims.
accepted_facts: Victims are found decapitated with notes typed on an old typewriter
Sir Gregory Penne owns an orangutan named Bhag who is trained and dangerous
Lawley Foss was blackmailing the Head-Hunter and was murdered
Adele Leamington was abducted and held prisoner at Griff Towers
inferred_conclusions: Sir Gregory Penne is the Head-Hunter murderer
Bhag the orangutan is responsible for the killings
Stella Mendoza is involved in the murders
mechanism_description: Sampson Longvale, inspired by his ancestor the executioner, is the Head-Hunter who murders victims using a guillotine hidden in caves beneath his house. He lures victims under various pretenses, restrains them with handcuffs, and executes them with the guillotine. The orangutan Bhag is used by Sir Gregory Penne for intimidation and kidnapping but is not the murderer. The murders are concealed by the remote location and the secret cave system.
delivery_path: Longvale receives letters from victims seeking help
Victims are brought to Dower House and restrained
Longvale uses the guillotine in the cave to execute victims
Heads are sent with typewritten notes from the Head-Hunter’s typewriter
Bhag and Penne are used as red herrings to mislead investigators
Adele Leamington is abducted but escapes into the caves
Michael Brixan uncovers the cave, guillotine, and Longvale’s identity
outcome_result: Sampson Longvale is revealed as the Head-Hunter murderer and dies by his own guillotine, while Sir Gregory Penne is imprisoned for related crimes.

false_assumption.statement: Sir Gregory Penne is the Head-Hunter murderer responsible for the decapitations.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Penne’s suspicious behavior, possession of the orangutan Bhag, and his violent past make him a natural suspect. The victims and clues are often found on or near his estate, implicating him.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the true murderer, Sampson Longvale, who operates independently using a hidden guillotine and manipulates events to frame Penne.

supporting_points: He owns the dangerous orangutan Bhag involved in abductions
He has a violent and suspicious past including assault
Bloodstained sword and missing sword found in his house
He was present at Griff Towers during key events
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He lacks the direct evidence and means to perform the guillotine executions in the hidden caves

red_herrings.description: Bhag, the trained orangutan servant of Sir Gregory Penne, is suspected of involvement in the crimes due to his intelligence and violent behavior.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Bhag is used by Penne for intimidation and kidnapping but is not capable of planning or committing the murders.

red_herrings.description: Lawley Foss, the scenario editor, is suspected due to his blackmail attempts against the Head-Hunter.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Foss was a victim who was murdered to silence his blackmail, not the perpetrator.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects are limited to the film studio company, the wealthy baronet and his associates, and the old gentleman Longvale, all of whom have access to the locations and potential motives.

time_anchors: Between eleven o’clock and three in the morning for Foss’s murder
Night and early morning hours for abductions and attacks
Daytime scenes at Griff Towers and studio
time_windows: Foss last seen alive at eleven pm
Adele abducted at night and escapes next day
Letters sent and collected on specific days
access_actors: Sir Gregory Penne (Griff Towers and orangutan)

Foss’s financial troubles and blackmail attempts

inference_path.effect: Penne is involved in crimes but not the Head-Hunter

Penne’s confession of killing a man in Borneo

inference_path.correction: Longvale is the Head-Hunter and murderer
inference_path.effect: Focus shifts to Longvale as the true culprit

inference_path.observation: Adele’s escape into the caves and discovery of guillotine
inference_path.correction: The caves are the murder site and hiding place
required_evidence: Adele’s lantern and discovery of bones in caves

inference_path.observation: Longvale restrains and prepares Michael for execution
inference_path.correction: Longvale’s capture and death by his own guillotine
required_evidence: Trapdoor and pulley mechanism in Dower House

discriminating_test.design: Michael Brixan arranges a sting by sending dummy letters to the Benefactor address and waits for the collection. He then uses the pulley trapdoor in Longvale’s house to capture him and observe his reaction and access to the guillotine. The test reveals Longvale’s guilt by his possession of the guillotine and his attempt to execute Michael.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The trap exposes Longvale as the Head-Hunter and murderer, confirming the guillotine as the murder weapon and the cave as the crime scene.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Longvale’s capture in the trapdoor and his possession of the guillotine equipment conclusively prove his guilt.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given access to all key clues: the peculiar typewritten notes, the presence of the guillotine and caves, the suspicious behavior of suspects, and the discovery of the handcuff fragment and butyl chloride. The narrative provides detailed observations and witness statements that allow deduction of the true murderer. The false solution implicates Penne, but inconsistencies and the final confession reveal the truth, enabling a careful reader to solve the mystery.
